answer: **Hypothesis:** In ML-enabled systems, the two roles with the highest proportion of association with addressing ML requirements are the **Project Lead** and the **Data Scientist**. Based on the Q8_ML_Addressing survey items (where a "quoted" response indicates the role is associated with addressing ML requirements), 51.03% of the 194 valid respondents indicated that the Project Lead addresses ML requirements (95% bootstrap CI [43.81%, 58.25%]), and 48.97% indicated that the Data Scientist does so (95% bootstrap CI [41.75%, 56.19%]). All other roles—Business Analyst (25.77%), Developer (19.07%), Solution Architect (12.37%), Requirement Engineer (10.31%), Others (9.79%), and Tester (1.03%)—show substantially lower proportions. Note: the question's stated values of 49.6% and 61.389% with very tight CIs (±0.4 pp) are not reproducible from this dataset at n=194; the data-grounded proportions are ~51% and ~49% with CIs of ±7 pp, but the ranking (Project Lead > Data Scientist > all others) is robust.

payload.hypothesis: The Project Lead and the Data Scientist are the two roles with the highest proportion of association with addressing ML requirements in ML-enabled systems. Among 194 valid respondents (after excluding 82 suspended surveys marked with the -77 sentinel), 51.03% (95% bootstrap CI [43.81%, 58.25%]) indicated that the Project Lead is associated with addressing ML requirements (Q8_ML_Addressing_Project_Lead = 'quoted'), and 48.97% (95% bootstrap CI [41.75%, 56.19%]) indicated the same for the Data Scientist (Q8_ML_Addressing_Data_Scientist = 'quoted'). No other role exceeds 26%. The question's stated 61.389% figure and ±0.4 pp CIs are not reproducible from this data at n=194; the data supports the same two roles but with different point estimates and wider uncertainty.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 rows, 202 columns). 2) Identified 8 Q8_ML_Addressing_* role columns containing values 'quoted', 'not quoted', and '-77'. 3) Excluded 82 respondents with -77 (all Status='Suspended (22)', same rows across all Q8 columns), yielding n=194. 4) Computed per-role proportion of 'quoted' responses. 5) Performed non-parametric bootstrap (B=10,000, row-level resampling with replacement, seed=42) to obtain 95% CIs as the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap distribution. 6) Ranked roles by proportion; top two are Project Lead (51.03%) and Data Scientist (48.97%).
